title: Eleven Adivasi tea garden residents arrested at Jaigaon land port site after 100-day protest
dek: About 80 families at Torsa Tea Garden in Alipurduar want compensation for land they have farmed for generations. A tea workers' union says the protest was peaceful and the charges should be dropped.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Police in Alipurduar have arrested 11 tea garden residents, all from Adivasi communities, after a confrontation at the site of a planned land port on the India-Bhutan border, where about 80 families had held a sit-in for more than 100 days demanding compensation and rehabilitation for land they say they have farmed for generations.

The arrests took place on Tuesday, 3 November, at Gotabari in the Torsa Tea Garden near Jaigaon, reports said. Four women and seven men were held. One report said that bulldozers razed the protest site, clearing the way for the Jaigaon land port being built by the Land Ports Authority of India (LPAI).

## The case

The first information report (Jaigaon police station case no. 326/26) was registered on 3 November on a written complaint dated 2 November from an LPAI junior engineer, one report said. It also names three activists, Anuradha Talwar, Binoy Kerkatta and Mahesh Xalxo, as having allegedly "provoked and instigated" the crowd; according to the report, none of the three was at the site. Relatives of those arrested said they did not know where they were for about 18 hours, during which they were moved between four or five police stations before the arrests were recorded.

The police and the district administration have not made a public statement on the arrests, and the charges in the FIR have not been published.

## The two sides

The Paschim Banga Cha Majoor Samity (PBCMS), a tea workers' union, said the families had protested peacefully beside the site for over 100 days without any police complaint. It said the confrontation began on 2 November when bulldozers arrived to work on disputed land without the families' demands being met. "There was no violence, assault or damage to government property. Protest and disagreement cannot be criminalised as violence," the union said in a statement. It has demanded the release of all 11, the withdrawal of charges, a halt to evictions and recognition of the workers' land rights.

The complaint on which the FIR is based came from the LPAI, the central authority building the port; the LPAI has not commented publicly. Construction at the site had been going on for about five months.

A fact-finding team including sociologist Virginius Xaxa visited Torsa on 1-3 August and found that families had cultivated the land for generations without ownership documents, reports said. The families have asked Bishal Lama, the Kalchini MLA and Minister of State for Home Affairs, to stop further evictions and secure the release of those held, according to another report.

## Why it matters

Land ports are customs and immigration posts that handle cross-border trucks and travellers. Jaigaon, opposite Phuentsholing, is the main gateway for trade between India and Bhutan, and a new port there is meant to ease congestion on the route. Most tea garden workers in north Bengal live on estate land without title, so land acquisition for infrastructure often leaves them with no legal claim to compensation, a long-running grievance in the Dooars.

Residents have started a fresh protest at the site against the arrests, reports said.
